📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-03-ms-scheduler-api-seriesid-negative-recordid`
This is occurrence #149 overall (first fire in ~17 days — longest dormancy on record for this entry). Degraded-mode alert (DD-scan-diff, no real Slack ts).
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `CRM Experience` (`@crm experience` / n/a)
Playbook: Confirm shape via DD monitor 303750093 Alert state OR ES fields.dd_service.keyword:"ms-scheduler-api" + exceptions.Message.keyword signature. 🚨 *new alert — needs human*  (score: 5)
Channel: alert-runtime-monitoring  •  bug-type guess: code  •  alerts in group: 1
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `CRM Experience` (`@customer-management` / `#team-customer-management`)

Symptoms:
  - default_web_site/reportgenerationapi P95 latency spiked to 73.3s (14.6x the 5s threshold), sustained 17:25:00-17:39:30Z UTC (~14 min) on PROD-REPORT-03
  - Account `portal1gnite`'s "MNGExport" report hit its 900s render timeout twice (17:39:06Z, 17:39:47Z); each time the aborted render thread survived `Thread.Abort()` and stayed stuck in native DevExpress/GDI+ code, holding its memory
  - Account `datamemorysales` hit an unrelated `NullReferenceException` during report disposal at 17:29:24Z, inside the same breach window

Trace IDs: 6a970a3600000000c1153a4105f49e9b, 6a970a5f00000000bd0f6675f3aaf34a
Likely cause: portal1gnite's MNGExport report is too slow/complex for the 900s timeout; Thread.Abort can't reliably kill the native rendering call, so the leaked thread starves the shared w3wp worker process's thread pool, dragging P95 latency up for every caller on that box during the window
Suggested next action: file defect (report-content perf review for MNGExport/portal1gnite + replace Thread.Abort-based timeout handling with a hard-kill/process-isolation strategy)

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-03-ms-scheduler-api-seriesid-negative-recordid`
This is occurrence #150 in the entry's history (every-10th-occurrence resurface — last notify was ~16h38m ago, still inside the 24h window on its own).
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `CRM Experience` (`@customer-management` / `#team-customer-management`)
Playbook: Confirm shape (DD monitor 303750093 Alert, or ES fields.dd_service.keyword:"ms-scheduler-api" AND fields.Account.keyword:<acct> "Failed to Get Series Id for record -1"). Compute error-rate ratio (historically marginal ~2.5-3%, do not over-escalate on monitor state alone). Root cause is a code-level missing-guard bug in SeriesDataProvider.GetSeriesIdAsync (recordId=-1 not guarded before SqlDataReader.GetValue()), reproduces across many accounts — file/bump a defect for CRM Experience rather than re-diagnosing from scratch.
Open Jira: n/a — fix_status still "proposed", no fix_jira on the entry after 150 occurrences
